name: Primary Products
definition: Named product categories and concrete examples; multi-select.
examples: Payroll software; industrial pumps; hamburgers

name: Primary Services
definition: Services sold to customers; distinguish services from internal support functions.
examples: Payroll processing; equipment maintenance; freight forwarding

name: Core Business Activity
definition: Precise operating verb + output; distinguish ownership, manufacturing, distribution and licensing.
examples: Manufactures pumps; licenses software; operates restaurants

name: Customer Type
definition: B2B / B2C / B2G / mixed; identify the paying customer separately from the end user.
examples: B2B employers; B2C diners; B2G agencies

name: Customer Segment
definition: Specific buyer/user populations and roles; do not substitute an industry or a customer-size claim.
examples: HR administrators; franchise operators; hospital procurement teams

name: End Markets
definition: Customer verticals or product applications; not the supplier’s own industry classification.
examples: Healthcare providers; automotive production; consumer dining

name: Customer Size
definition: SMB / mid-market / enterprise / government / consumer / mixed; retain issuer definitions.
examples: SMB employers; large enterprises; individual consumers

name: Business Model
definition: How operations are organized and value is delivered; distinguish from billing.
examples: Franchisor; vertically integrated manufacturer; marketplace operator

name: Revenue Model
definition: What customers pay for and how revenue is earned; preserve multiple streams.
examples: Subscription fees; product sales; transaction commissions

name: Value Chain Position
definition: Position in the supply/value chain and role relative to customers and suppliers.
examples: Component supplier; OEM; wholesale distributor

name: Geography Served
definition: Markets actually served; distinguish customers/operations from headquarters.
examples: U.S. customers; Europe and Asia; domestic-only operations

name: Product Specialization
definition: Breadth and focus of offerings, distinct from a product list or an unverified superiority claim.
examples: Single therapeutic area; broad HCM suite; application-specific components

name: Distribution Channels
definition: How customers are reached and sales/orders acquired.
examples: Direct sales; independent distributors; e-commerce

name: Delivery Model
definition: How the product/service is provided or deployed; distinguish from acquisition channel.
examples: Cloud SaaS; on-premise installation; on-site managed service

name: Pricing Structure
definition: Charging unit and contractual pricing mechanism; avoid securities/debt pricing.
examples: Per employee/month; fixed project fee; cost-plus contract

name: Recurring Revenue Profile
definition: Nature of repeat revenue; distinguish contracted recurrence from habitual repeat purchases.
examples: Renewable subscriptions; usage-based recurring fees; repeat noncontractual purchases

name: Customer Concentration
definition: Named large-customer dependence or disclosed concentration; include period and denominator for figures.
examples: Largest customer: 15% of annual revenue; diversified customer base

name: Contract Duration
definition: Customer/service/franchise contract term and renewal structure; exclude financing maturities.
examples: Annual auto-renewal; three-year service term; month-to-month

name: Capital Intensity
definition: Owned/leased productive assets and investment needs; distinguish issuer assets from franchisee/supplier assets.
examples: Owned factories; leased retail sites; outsourced production

name: Regulatory Exposure
definition: Applicable operating licenses, approvals and regulatory regimes; identify jurisdiction.
examples: FDA device clearance; banking supervision; food-safety regulation

name: Customer Switching Costs
definition: Cited operational, contractual or integration barriers; do not assume high costs from tenure alone.
examples: Data migration; workflow retraining; contractual termination fees

name: Company Size Category
definition: Supplier operating scale with dated evidence and units; not customer size or an unsupported size label.
examples: 2,000 employees; 300 operated stores; annual revenue in stated currency

name: Labor Intensity
definition: Dependence on labor, specialist personnel or billable capacity.
examples: Clinician-led care; technician-intensive service; automated production

name: Revenue Cyclicality
definition: Documented demand sensitivity, seasonality or cycle exposure; distinguish observed history from inference.
examples: Construction-cycle demand; holiday seasonality; commodity-linked demand

name: Supply Chain Complexity
definition: Sourcing dependencies, concentration, lead times and procurement structure.
examples: Single-source component; global supplier network; cooperative purchasing

name: Technology Dependence
definition: Operational reliance on technology/platforms; being in technology is not proof of a specific dependency.
examples: Third-party cloud infrastructure; proprietary transaction platform

name: Geographic Concentration
definition: Dependence on particular markets; distinguish from the list of countries served.
examples: 80% of annual revenue in the U.S.; concentrated in one state

name: Product Differentiation
definition: Specific product/service differences with evidence; label issuer marketing claims.
examples: Patented process; industry-specific workflow; custom-engineered design

name: IP Dependence
definition: Material dependence on patents, licenses, proprietary technology or other protected rights.
examples: Licensed drug rights; patent-protected process; proprietary software

name: Brand Dependence
definition: Role of brand, trademark, licensing and customer recognition; distinguish documented model from assumed brand strength.
examples: Licensed consumer brand; branded franchise system; private-label supplier

name: Competitive Positioning
definition: Attributable positioning/share claims with date, geography and market definition; label self-descriptions.
examples: Issuer-described niche leader; independently measured category share

name: Company Maturity
definition: Operating stage and relevant business history; incorporation date alone does not establish maturity.
examples: Commercial-stage business; pre-revenue development; established operating platform
